# BRC Analytics Federated Service — Status Report

## Abstract
This report addresses a single operational question: is the BRC Analytics federated MCP service currently reachable, and what functional limitations does it carry. The `brc_federation_status` diagnostic tool was queried directly against the live BRC Analytics API (`https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/`). The service reported version 0.29.0 running in the production environment, with health status "healthy" as of timestamp 2026-09-17T21:23:59.788257. The service is reachable (`reachable: true`). Five known limitations were returned, covering two broken federated tools (`search_ena_keywords`, `search_ena`), one broken native endpoint (`/api/v1/ena/study/{accession}`), a scope limitation of the catalog tools (no resistance phenotype data, only two E. coli assemblies), and a URL-formatting trap on the MCP endpoint itself (missing trailing slash triggers an https-to-http downgrade redirect that MCP clients refuse). Each limitation carries a verified date of 2026-09-17 and a recommended workaround tool. This result matters because several of these failure modes return HTTP error text disguised as ordinary tool output, which could be mistaken for a valid empty or negative result rather than a service defect.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** BRC Analytics aggregates genome assembly, ENA sequencing-run, and workflow-compatibility data for bacterial and other reference collections, exposed through a federated MCP tool layer that this assistant calls alongside NCBI, UniProt, and STRING resources.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before this call, it was unknown whether the BRC Analytics backend was live, and which of its federated tools return reliable data versus silent failures.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine current service reachability and enumerate documented tool-level limitations. No biological hypothesis applies; this is an infrastructure status check.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** A single diagnostic call was routed to the tool purpose-built for this check, rather than probing individual BRC tools indirectly.

**Materials.** BRC Analytics production API, queried via the `brc_federation_status` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call was made: `brc_federation_status` with no arguments (the tool accepts none). The call returned the MCP URL, live version/health payloads, a reachability flag, and a `known_limitations` array.

**Statistical Analysis.** Not applicable; this is a categorical status/limitations report with no counts requiring derivation, deduplication, or denominators.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

Table 1. Service status

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| MCP URL | https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/ |
| Version | 0.29.0 |
| Environment | production |
| Health status | healthy |
| Reachable | true |
| Timestamp | 2026-09-17T21:23:59.788257 |

Table 2. Known limitations

| # | Affected tool/endpoint | Problem | Recommended alternative | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `search_ena_keywords` | Sends an unquoted scientific_name to ENA; ENA answers HTTP 400. The failure is returned as tool text, so it can read like an answer. | `brc_ena_search` | 2026-09-17 |
| 2 | `search_ena` | Caps at 50 rows with `has_more: true`, and never reports a total. | `brc_ena_runs` | 2026-09-17 |
| 3 | `/api/v1/ena/study/{accession}` | Answers HTTP 500 for every accession tried. | `brc_ena_study` | 2026-09-17 |
| 4 | All catalog tools | Catalog holds no resistance phenotypes and only 2 E. coli assemblies (K-12 MG1655, O157:H7 Sakai). Answers "what can I compute, on which genome," not "how many resistant strains exist." | State the gap plainly; route phenotype questions to BV-BRC or CARD | 2026-09-17 |
| 5 | MCP endpoint itself | `https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp` (no trailing slash) answers 307 to a plain `http://` URL; MCP client refuses the https-to-http downgrade, surfacing as an HTTP error. | Always call the slashed URL | 2026-09-17 |

**Findings.** The service is live and healthy (version 0.29.0, production). Five limitations were reported: two federated ENA-search tools, one native ENA-study endpoint, a scope constraint on all catalog tools (2 E. coli assemblies, no AMR phenotype data), and a URL-formatting issue on the base MCP endpoint.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The service currently meets basic reachability and health criteria. However, three of five limitations manifest as text that can be mistaken for a genuine answer (HTTP 400/500 errors returned as tool output, or an artificially low result count with no stated total), which is a functional risk beyond simple downtime.

**Context.** No external literature bears on this operational question; findings rest entirely on the single diagnostic payload retrieved.

**Limitations.** This report reflects a single point-in-time check (2026-09-17); it does not confirm the underlying data content of BRC Analytics' catalog beyond the stated two-assembly E. coli scope, and it does not verify fixes to any of the five listed issues beyond their "verified" date.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** The BRC Analytics MCP service is reachable and healthy, but callers should avoid `search_ena_keywords`, `search_ena`, and the unslashed MCP URL, and should not expect resistance-phenotype data from any catalog tool. A useful next check would be re-running `brc_federation_status` at a later date to see whether any of the five listed issues have been resolved.

## References
[1] BRC Analytics API — `brc_federation_status` tool result, MCP URL: https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/

## Acknowledgments
Data provider: BRC Analytics (https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/), production API version 0.29.0.
